title: Stem-changers and yo-irregulars in the subjunctive
summary: Stem-changing verbs keep their boot in the subjunctive, -ir verbs change nosotros and vosotros too, and odd yo forms carry over: conozca, traiga, oiga.
focus: Forming the present subjunctive of stem-changing and yo-irregular verbs
content:
## The boot stays: -ar and -er verbs

Stem-changing verbs keep their change in the subjunctive. For **-ar** and **-er** verbs it sits in the same "boot" as in the present. **Yo, tú, él** and **ellos** change, while **nosotros** and **vosotros** keep the plain stem.

| | pensar (e → ie) | volver (o → ue) |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **piense** | **vuelva** |
| tú | **pienses** | **vuelvas** |
| él / ella / usted | **piense** | **vuelva** |
| nosotros/as | pensemos | volvamos |
| vosotros/as | penséis | volváis |
| ellos / ustedes | **piensen** | **vuelvan** |

**Querer** (quiera, queramos) and **poder** (pueda, podamos) work the same way.

## -ir verbs change outside the boot too

Stem-changing **-ir** verbs add a small change in **nosotros** and **vosotros**: **e → i** and **o → u**.

| | sentir (e → ie / i) | dormir (o → ue / u) | pedir (e → i) |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | sienta | duerma | pida |
| tú | sientas | duermas | pidas |
| él / ella / usted | sienta | duerma | pida |
| nosotros/as | **sintamos** | **durmamos** | **pidamos** |
| vosotros/as | **sintáis** | **durmáis** | **pidáis** |
| ellos / ustedes | sientan | duerman | pidan |

**Pedir** keeps its **i** in every form. Never *dormamos* or *pedamos*.

## The yo stem carries over

Take the **yo** form of the present, drop the **-o**, add the subjunctive ending. Whatever is odd about the yo form travels with it:

- conozco → **conozca, conozcas, conozcamos…**
- traigo → **traiga, traigas, traigamos…**
- oigo → **oiga, oigas, oigamos…**

You already know this pattern from the imperative: **tengo → tenga**, **hago → haga**, **salgo → salga**, **pongo → ponga**, **digo → diga**, **vengo → venga**. Only the endings change from person to person, and the stem stays the same.

## Practise with ojalá and quiero que

Two triggers are enough to practise every form.

- **Ojalá** + subjunctive expresses a wish. *Ojalá vuelvas pronto.* (I hope you come back soon.)
- **Quiero que** + subjunctive is used when someone else does the action. *Quiero que conozcas a mi hermana.* (I want you to meet my sister.)
- *Ojalá durmamos bien en el tren.* (I hope we sleep well on the train.)
- *Mis padres quieren que traigamos el postre.* (My parents want us to bring dessert.)
- *Quiero que pidáis lo que queráis.* (I want you all to order whatever you like.)

Same subject? Use the infinitive: **quiero dormir**, not *quiero que duerma*.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá pienses en mí durante el viaje.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you think of me during the trip.
I hope we come back to this restaurant.

vocabulary.example: Quiero que los niños duerman la siesta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want the children to have a nap.
I hope they don't ask for more money.

vocabulary.example: Quiero que os sintáis como en casa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want you all to feel at home.

vocabulary.meaning: to know, to meet (a person, a place)
vocabulary.example: Quiero que conozcas a mi mejor amiga.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want you to meet my best friend.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el camarero traiga pan pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the waiter brings bread soon.

vocabulary.example: Habla más alto: quiero que todos te oigan.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Speak up: I want everyone to hear you.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá haga buen tiempo el domingo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the weather is good on Sunday.

vocabulary.example: Quiero que vengas conmigo al cine.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want you to come to the cinema with me.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá mi hermano ___ pronto de Londres. (volver)
quiz.explanation: Él is inside the boot, so o → ue: vuelva. 'Vuelve' is the indicative; 'volva' does not exist.
hints: o changes to ue, then the -er verb takes -a.

quiz.prompt: Mis padres quieren que (nosotros) ___ (volver) antes de las diez.
quiz.explanation: Volver is an -er verb: nosotros stays outside the boot and keeps the plain stem: volvamos.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá ___ bien esta noche, que mañana madrugamos. (dormir, nosotros)
quiz.explanation: Dormir is an -ir verb, so nosotros changes o → u: durmamos.

quiz.prompt: Quiero que (tú) ___ (pedir) la cuenta, por favor.
quiz.explanation: Pedir changes e → i in every subjunctive form: pidas.

quiz.prompt: Quiero que ___ a mi novia este fin de semana. (conocer, vosotros)
quiz.explanation: The yo form is conozco, so the stem is conozc- in every person: conozcáis.
hints: Start from the yo form: conozco.

quiz.explanation: Poder is an o → ue verb and tú is in the boot: puedas.

quiz.prompt: ¿Quieres que te ___ un café de la máquina? (traer, yo)
quiz.explanation: Traigo becomes traiga because the -ig- of the yo form carries over.
hints: What is 'I bring' in the present?

quiz.prompt: No quiero que (vosotros) ___ (sentir) miedo en el avión.
quiz.explanation: Sentir is an -ir verb: vosotros changes e → i and carries the accent: sintáis.

quiz.prompt: No quiero que (tú) ___ (pensar) que estoy enfadado.
quiz.explanation: Tú is inside the boot, so e → ie: pienses.
hints: e changes to ie, then add -es.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá los vecinos no ___ la música desde su casa. (oír)
quiz.explanation: Oigo becomes oiga because the yo stem oig- carries over, so ellos is oigan.

conversations.title: Dinner with the family
conversations.scenario: Lucía has invited her boyfriend Javier to a family dinner on Saturday, and he is a little nervous.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Javier, ¿vienes a la cena del sábado?
lines.meaning: Javier, are you coming to Saturday's dinner?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ojalá pueda, pero trabajo hasta las ocho.
lines.meaning: I hope I can, but I work until eight.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Mis padres quieren que conozcas a toda la familia.
lines.meaning: My parents want you to meet the whole family.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: How nerve-racking! Do you want me to bring anything?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, quiero que traigas el postre.
lines.meaning: Yes, I want you to bring dessert.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale. ¿Y quieres que pida un taxi para volver?
lines.meaning: OK. And do you want me to order a taxi to get back?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No, mi madre quiere que durmáis en casa, tú y tu hermano.
lines.meaning: No, my mother wants you to sleep at our place, you and your brother.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Perfecto. Ojalá no pensemos en el trabajo en todo el fin de semana.
lines.meaning: Perfect. I hope we don't think about work all weekend.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ojalá. Y ojalá mi abuela no te haga demasiadas preguntas.
lines.meaning: Let's hope so. And I hope my grandmother doesn't ask you too many questions.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tranquila: quiero que tu familia me quiera.
lines.meaning: Don't worry: I want your family to love me.

listening.meaning: I hope you come home soon.
listening.note: Tú is in the boot: o → ue.

listening.text: Quiero que duermas un poco más.
listening.meaning: I want you to sleep a little more.

listening.text: Ojalá podamos ver el partido juntos.
listening.meaning: I hope we can watch the match together.
listening.note: Nosotros of poder has no stem change.

listening.text: Mi madre quiere que conozcáis a su vecina.
listening.meaning: My mother wants you all to meet her neighbour.

listening.text: Quiero que traigas el paraguas porque va a llover.
listening.meaning: I want you to bring the umbrella because it's going to rain.
listening.note: New word: el paraguas = the umbrella.

listening.text: No quiero que sintáis vergüenza por vuestro acento.
listening.meaning: I don't want you all to feel embarrassed about your accent.

listening.text: Quiero que oigas esta canción antes de la fiesta.
listening.meaning: I want you to hear this song before the party.

listening.text: Ojalá que los niños duerman bien y no pidan agua a medianoche.
listening.meaning: I hope the children sleep well and don't ask for water at midnight.

guide.tip: Say the yo, tú, él and ellos forms in a column and you draw the boot. Everything inside it changes. For -ir verbs, nosotros and vosotros also get the small change from e to i or from o to u.

bites.title: Inside the boot
bites.rule: -ar and -er stem-changers change in yo, tú, él and ellos, just like the present. Nosotros and vosotros keep the plain stem.
bites.example_meaning: I hope you come back. I hope we come back.

bites.title: -ir verbs: one step more
bites.rule: -ir stem-changers also change nosotros and vosotros, from e to i and from o to u: durmamos, sintáis, pidamos.

bites.title: The yo stem travels
bites.rule: Start from the yo form of the present and keep its oddity: conozco gives conozca, traigo gives traiga, oigo gives oiga, tengo gives tenga.
bites.example_meaning: I want you to meet Ana.

sorts.title: Does nosotros change?
sorts.why: -ar and -er verbs keep the plain stem in nosotros; -ir stem-changers switch to i or u.

sorts.title: Where does the change come from?
sorts.why: Boot verbs change the vowel, while verbs like conocer, traer, oír and tener copy the yo form of the present.

spots.why: Pensar is an -ar verb: nosotros is outside the boot.

spots.sentence: Quiero que dormamos en la playa.
spots.why: Dormir is an -ir verb: nosotros changes o → u.

spots.sentence: Quiero que conoces a mi hermana.
spots.why: Quiero que with another subject takes the subjunctive, built on conozco.

spots.sentence: Mi padre quiere que pedáis la paella.
spots.why: Pedir has i in every subjunctive form.
Ojalá takes the subjunctive: traigo gives traigas.
